If you really want to make money in the stock market you need to stop thinking like a consumer.  I like to sell puts in all types of assets.  I look for a asset that isn't going anywhere.  You can do stock like tesla or to commodities like coffee or to assets like gold & silver.  By selling the puts I put up the liquidity and act like insurance.  I do it short term around 90 days but sometimes I will do a year.  Despite if im down I always roll it and collect the higher premiums.  I always make money because of theta/ time.  I then use the premiums to buy cash flowing assets.  
 Warren buffett makes almost 4 billion a year from selling puts and buying up stock or other assets.  Why would you buy into the s&p trying to make 10 roi a year when someone will pay you 10% for putting up the liquidity.  Yes if it goes down you might lose some liquidity.  But  in the long run the stock market biggest crashes lasted by 2 to 4 years before a 30% comeback.  I put 5% into each investment.  Even if there was a chance of me losing half my money on a investment it wouldn't be but 2.5 % of my portfolio.
